---
title: "How to check whether your items measure the factors you assumed"
description: "Explore whether your items group into the factors you expected."
---

Explore whether your items group into the factors you expected.

The example in this guide is *Employee engagement at work*. An employee engagement survey of 8 items, written to measure 2 things employees judge: how their work is organised, and the content of their work.

## In SurveyStudio

1. In RStudio, open the **Addins** menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo** and pick `factor_structure`.
2. On **Design**, see the 8 items written for 2 constructs.
3. On **Design**, choose **Plan**. RQ1 checks whether the data suit factor analysis, and RQ2 estimates the factors and the items that load on each.
4. On **Analyse**, run the plan and compare the loadings with the structure you expected.

![The Design screen with the Employee engagement at work study open.](../../templates/factor_structure/design.png){width=100%}

## In R

```r
d <- sframe_demo("factor_structure")
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
```

## The research questions and what the report gives

| Research question | Method | What the report gives |
|---|---|---|
| Is this data suitable for factor analysis? | Factorability checks (KMO and Bartlett's test) | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |
| How many factors, and which items load where? | Exploratory factor analysis | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |

Run the example in SurveyStudio or R to see the results, each marked as demonstration data.
